newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 per tonne lower on Wednesday, as traders expected the market to continue to consolidate recent sharp gains, traders said.

They said an increase in margins may pressure the spot month, but otherwise was not expected to have much of an effect on the market. The CSCE announced after Tuesday's close it will raise margins on all cocoa contracts by $100, to $600, effective today.
"It may have an impact on the spot month," said one trader. "But to the main players, a $100-increase is not going to make a difference."

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended mainly weaker, after an early rally to new eight-highs ran into origin sales and profit takers. September ended $4 a tonne lower, at $1,625, after ranging from a lifetime high of $1,655 and $1,598.
Spot July rose $3, to $1,584, after rallying to a new high of $1,620 -- the highest spot price on a continuous weekly chart since 1989. The remaining contracts finished $7 to $13 lower.

Some traders said the market was still overbought and that September may have to fill a $1,540-$1,516 chart gap formed last Thursday, before the market could make further gains. In the near-term, they said September support was seen near today's low at $1,598.
On the fundamental side, traders in Indonesia are keeping an eye on the El Nino weather pattern, but said it was too early to speculate on how it would affect cocoa production.

In London, cocoa futures were higher early Wednesday, buoyed by switch and option-linked buying. LIFFE September was up nine stg at the midday break, to 1,120 stg, while spot July climbed 11 stg, to 1,102 stg.
